name: Chic-Chocs and McGerrigle Mountains (Appalachians of the Gaspé)
description: The highest part of the Canadian Appalachians, in the interior of the Gaspé Peninsula: Mont Jacques-Cartier (1,268 m), Mont de la Passe (1,242 m), Mont Albert (1,181 m). Alpine summits rise above the forest.

sources.title: Table 15.3 Selected principal heights, by province and territory (Canada Year Book 2010, archived; source: NRCan Atlas of Canada)

limitations: Only heights are verified from an official table; landscape description is agent-04 interpretation pending a Parc national de la Gaspésie (Sépaq) source.
